content.title: What will air in place of ‘The Bachelorette’ after cancellation?
content.text: ABC decided to scrap season 22 of “The Bachelorette” just three days before its Sunday, March 22 premiere. So, what will air in the reality show’s place?A rerun of an “American Idol” episode will air on ABC at 8 p.m. ET on March 22 in place of “The Bachelorette” season 22 premiere. The episode, which features performances from the top 20 contestants, originally aired on Monday, March 16.ABC has not yet announced what will fill the Sunday 8 p.m. ET time slot moving forward. ABC’s decision to cancel the season came hours after TMZ published shocking footage of season 22 Bachelorette Taylor Frankie Paul on Thursday, March 19. The footage, which was recorded in 2023, showed Paul, 31, kicking and throwing metal stools at her then-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen. One of the chairs struck Paul’s daughter Indy, then 5.“In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family,” a spokesperson for Disney Entertainment Television said in a statement shared with NJ.com. Paul was arrested following the 2023 incident. She entered a plea in abeyance to a third-degree felony count of aggravated assault that August. Other charges, including criminal mischief and commission of domestic violence in the presence of a child, were dropped. The terms of the plea in abeyance required Paul to avoid violating the law for 36 months. She was set to have a review for the case this upcoming August.Paul’s 2023 arrest was discussed on season 1 of the Hulu reality show “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives,” which premiered in 2024.How did Taylor Frankie Paul react to the video leaking?After TMZ published the video, a spokesperson for Paul told NBC News that the leak was the “latest installment of [Mortensen’s] never-ending, desperate, attention-seeking, destructive campaign to harm Taylor without any regard for the consequences for their child.”“Releasing an old video, which conveniently omits context, on their son’s birthday is a reprehensible attempt to distract from his own behavior,” the spokesperson continued. “Thankfully, the public has seen this act before and knows who he is and sadly, many will recognize this pattern of manipulation, both in his actions on the show, and from their own experiences.”READ MORE: ABC will pay a high price for suddenly canceling ‘The Bachelorette:’ See how muchAfter ABC canceled “The Bachelorette,” a rep for Paul said she is “finally gaining the strength to face her accuser and taking steps to ensure that she and her children are protected from any further harm” after “years of silently suffering extensive mental and physical abuse as well as threats of retaliation.”In a statement of his own shared with Entertainment Weekly, Mortensen said: “As anyone who has seen the video will understand, this is a deeply upsetting situation. I am, unfortunately, used to these baseless claims about me and our relationship, which I categorically deny. I am focusing on our son and his safety, and hope that Taylor will do the same.”Dakota Mortensen and Taylor Frankie Paul.DisneyPaul shares son Ever, 2, with Mortensen. She also shares daughter Indy, 8, and son Ocean, 5, with her ex-husband, Tate Paul. Paul and Mortensen are the subjects of an ongoing domestic violence investigationWhile the TMZ video is from three years ago, Paul and Mortensen accused each other of domestic violence more recently. Mortensen was granted a protective order and temporary custody of Ever on Friday, March 20. A hearing has been set for Apr. 7.According to TMZ, Mortensen alleged that Paul choked him, shoved him and struck him on Feb. 23, 2026. He also claimed that Paul’s “aggressive behavior” woke up their son, Ever.Allegations were made “in both directions,” a spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People.READ MORE: Reality star breaks silence on shocking domestic violence claims: ‘There’s more to the story’Did ABC know about the Taylor Frankie Paul video before it leaked? NBC recently obtained audio of a March 7, 2026, Zoom call in which cast members from “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” raised concerns to Disney executives about continuing to film with Paul in the wake of the recent allegations against her and Mortensen. The Walt Disney Company owns both ABC and Hulu. According to NBC, several cast members repeatedly mentioned “distressing” and “upsetting” recordings of Paul’s alleged conduct, but did not play the videos on the call.
